crime_highlights: S.M.P. told S.S. to come to his bedroom
S.M.P. pinned her down by holding her wrists during the penetrative offences
the offences were committed with aggressive, painful, force
S.S. recalled feeling such intense pain after these incidents that it caused her to stumble as she was leaving S.M.P.'s bedroom
rationale_highlights: I agree with counsel for the defence that the Gladue letter confirms S.M.P. is a person who comes before the court in circumstances where his life has been severely and negatively impacted by the effects of colonization and the systemic marginalization of Indigenous people in our country's history
the many Gladue factors applicable to S.M.P., including the trauma he experienced while attending two Residential Schools, play a meaningful role in sentencing him
they do somewhat diminish his level of moral blameworthiness for the offences against S.S.
Absent the Gladue factors and experiences as an Indigenous person that apply to S.M.P., I would have found that the circumstances justified a high mid-single-digit sentence

crime_highlights: Mr. Campbell has admitted to being one of the three males who entered Mr. Goldstein's basement suite in the early morning hours of April 6, 2022, confronting and confining him
One of the three males shot Mr. Goldstein
The three males fled, taking property from the home as they did so
the shooting death of David Goldstein on April 6, 2022, at his home in Surrey
rationale_highlights: Section 718.2(e) of the Code states explicitly that sentencing courts must apply the principle of restraint with particular attention to the personal circumstances of Indigenous offenders
Here, I take into account the unique, systemic and background factors that may have played a part in bringing Mr. Campbell before the court
a number of adverse factors that affect Indigenous persons in general because of systemic discrimination are specifically present

I must also consider Mr. Campbell's rehabilitation, in particular his modest age, his guilty plea, his Métis status and the background factors that have brought him before the court as part of his prospects for rehabilitation
note: Court's stated effect is mitigating factor (para 36) and rehabilitation; joint submission accepted.

crime_highlights: J. was very young and highly vulnerable to the abuse which she experienced at the hands of her father, who was in a position of trust
Mr. B-B. took advantage of his close personal relationship with J. and told her keep the abuse a secret
J. was fearful of disclosing the abuse
Mr. B-B. did not stop abusing J. on his own volition; rather he only stopped the sexual abuse after J. reported it
Mr. B-B. put his sexual gratification ahead of J.'s needs
rationale_highlights: background or systemic factors that may have contributed to Mr. B-B. appearing before the court and which thus diminish his moral blameworthiness
The Gladue factors here include a traumatic childhood where he was subjected to physical abuse, sexual abuse, and witnessed violence against his mother
mitigate some of Mr. B-B.'s blameworthiness in accordance with the Glaude principles
